title: Classify the signed permutations that split every c=3 centre character.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Finite exact certificate for sector `c=3` of the historical one-slot doubled centre operator. The residual coordinate signed permutations that split every sign character of that block are 96 explicit involutions. One commuting pair splits each of the 16 characters into four positive `A_3`-invariant joint eigenspaces. The trivial character splits as `216+216+216+216`.

Two claim types are kept apart in `research/c3-centre-sign-split/PROOF.md`:

- **Proof.** The support automorphisms are `AGL(3,2)`. The eight coordinate sign flips and five affine generators are orthogonal linear symmetries and generate every signed affine map, a group of order `344064`. The orbit of label `3` has size 112, so the stabilizer has order `3072`. The explicit involutions `u=(0 2)(4 6)` and `v=(0 4)(2 6)`, with the stated signs, commute with `A_3`, and the trace formula gives the joint dimensions below.
- **Exhaustive finite census.** `T(3)` was evaluated on all `344064` signed affine maps. The `3072` hits were rebuilt with the full port check. The scalar-conjugation test on every stabilizer element finds exactly 128 elements that preserve every character. Ninety-six of them split every character; the other 32 are diagonal signs and act by a scalar. This is not a partial search, and it is not a proof about symmetries outside this signed-permutation group.

No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`. This is not an annihilating polynomial and does not replace the degree-881 one-slot certificate.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (priority revision 8). This fork draft is based on the pin of that commit, `cursor/upstream-7c49fe32-pin-20de`, because the fork's `main` is not upstream main.
- Handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144258
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6944, head `26ceb7a0b4e04d4377a31aaa849dcb13e06e4cbc`. That PR splits preserved characters of `c=1` and `c=128` and records that `g` sends sector 3 to 343. Its open question includes every character of `c=3`. This package answers only that clause.
- Package: `research/c3-centre-sign-split/`
- Live query: `research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/frozen/work/centre-encoding-campaign-20261014/lanes/circuit-interface/INTERFACE.json`, SHA256 `5c6c51fbffc07a683e922f17532fd90262ae9e23cc3560a696002073dd234ef3`, git blob `4201e9a04c12273b919e2cae60a6b6482c8150f3`.

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. The handoff's c=3 clause asks which residual signed permutations split every character of sector 3. The predecessor pair does not act on that block.

Overlap refresh on 2026-11-10: 895 open PRs and 6934 discussion records, pagination complete; local notes complete at the upstream base. No open PR claims a splitter that preserves sector 3. The c=1 characters moved by `g` and `t`, the characteristic polynomial of a 216-dimensional `A_1` block, and the irreducibility of that block are different questions and are not taken here.

The pair is `u = (0 2)(4 6)` with minus signs on coordinates 0 and 2, and `v = (0 4)(2 6)` with minus signs on coordinates 0 and 4. Both square to the identity and commute. Their product is `(0 6)(2 4)` with minus signs on coordinates 0 and 6. All three fix sector 3. Joint dimensions by character weight:

| weight | dimension | joint dimensions |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 864 | 216, 216, 216, 216 |
| 1 | 432 | 180, 84, 84, 84 |
| 2 | 192 | 48, 48, 48, 48 |
| 3 | 80 | 44, 12, 12, 12 |
| 4 | 32 | 8, 8, 8, 8 |

`g` still sends sector 3 to 343. `t` fixes sector 3 and preserves only 8 of the 16 characters.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/c3-centre-sign-split/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/c3-centre-sign-split/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c3-centre-sign-split --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_C3_CENTRE_SIGN_SPLIT`. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

Rejection controls: a coordinate transposition is rejected; the double transposition `(0 2)(4 6)` with minus signs on all four even coordinates is a symmetry but sends sector 3 to 48; dropping one sign no longer reproduces dimension 864.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the degree-410 minor, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions and the open c=3 question. Upstream PR #6944 is the c=1/c=128 split that isolates this clause. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. Krzysztof Wojt's PR5168 is the degree-881 one-slot annihilator. The doubled representation comes from PR1719.

## Open next questions

- Characteristic polynomial of one 16-dimensional joint summand of the weight-4 `c=3` character. The trace formula gives dimension 8 for each joint space of that character and does not list a basis. This is not the 216-dimensional `A_1` block.
- Whether one payload involution from the degree-881 certificate fixes sector 3 and splits a joint space further. Those operators are outside the signed-permutation group classified here.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The predecessor certificate already names the blocker, `g` sends sector 3 to 343, so the next session can start from the stabilizer of sector 3 instead of reusing that pair. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
